A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 42-page FLOCK paper, including Appendices A–I. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical scientific material; only author affiliation and arXiv version/date information on page 1 differ.

before.justification: v2 reports original PETALS experiments, entity and relation prediction across 54 knowledge graphs, ablations, and additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–12 and the scaling, embedding, and graph-sparsity analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain identical random-walk sampling, anonymization, sequence processing, consensus, and inference procedures. The training objectives in Appendix I are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pretraining datasets, 54 evaluation knowledge graphs, entity and relation prediction tasks, and 220 PETALS instances. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments: ULTRA and TRIX in the main benchmark comparisons, MOTIF additionally on PETALS, and TRIX with noise injection in Appendix F.

E3.justification: The evaluation splits, filtered-ranking protocol, metrics, training budgets, preprocessing, and inference settings are unchanged, including the detailed settings in Appendix I and Tables 13–19.

E4.justification: The scaling and component ablations in Sections 5.3–5.4, scalability measurements, noise-injection comparison, METAFAM case study, and sparsity analysis in Appendices E–H are identical.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the Pearson-correlation significance analysis in Figure 7 and Appendix H. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results, rankings, and qualitative findings are identical, including appendix results. For example, FLOCK's total zero-shot MRR remains 0.391 for entity prediction in Table 2 and 0.881 for relation prediction in Table 3.

T1.justification: The definitions in Section 3, Propositions 4.1–4.3, all Appendix B proofs, and the mathematical formulations and complexity analysis elsewhere are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims concerning probabilistic equivariance, universal approximation, limitations of existing KGFMs, and empirical performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving walk coverage, joint entity–relation encoding, structured randomness, and graph sparsity are unchanged. The scalability limitation and future directions in Section 6 are also identical.

D1.justification: Implementation details, PETALS generation instructions, hardware and timing disclosures, and hyperparameter tables are identical. The code and checkpoint release statements and repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and the reference list are identical. Positioning relative to message-passing KGFMs and prior stochastic graph models is unchanged.

P1.justification: On page 1, İsmail İlkan Ceylan's affiliation superscript changes from 3,4 to 3,4,2, adding the University of Oxford. The arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 17 February 2026 to v3 dated 8 May 2026. Scientific prose and document organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–19 retain identical displays, captions, and placement. The affiliation and version-stamp edits introduce no layout reorganization; rendered pages 2–42 are pixel-identical.

improvement.justification: v3 updates an author affiliation and the version/date stamp. The scientific content, supporting evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful change in overall paper quality.
